sections: S&P monthly chart – April monthly bar just opened, but the range traveled merits zooming out. Monthly trend hasn't changed to down. The higher low to watch is ~480 at the prior pivot high, support trend line, 50 SMA, and 50% fib.

S&P weekly chart – The trend is clearly down, with the large liquidation on Thursday & Friday closing below a HVN and anchored VWAP references. We can see decent confluence at the 480 level if losses extend there. If markets rally, we cant discount a possible weekly lower high under 550.

S&P daily chart – For a v-shaped capitulation recovery, markets need a failure under Friday's low (or any subsequent highly correlated low) or fail to get acceptance lower on a gap down. Structural lows can develop once volatility has passed.
S&P hourly chart – Best to approach with caution. A counter trend may develop, but it likely won't change the major trend just yet. Bears undoubtably have the upper hand still.

Market internals – The reads here are the most extreme we've seen since the covid crash. This starts to feel like capitulation when we have such high degrees of correlation. My only concern is that the intraday sell off structure on Friday was fairly orderly. Panic would be better.

Market profile – Profile isn't very useful in high vol outside of day timeframe analysis. The most important note is simply the PoC slammed into Friday LoD. Suggests an open above has the potential to pinch out shorts.
